title: Always stay on top” behavior not working correctly

judgment.rationale: A maintainer has already asked which application should be above the Dock and whether the setup is multi-monitor; no reporter response is present. The issue is labeled Needs-Author-Feedback, and the existing reproduction artifact predates this newer request. Do not post a duplicate request or treat the earlier generic reproduction as current.
evidence: The original report identifies Command Palette Dock 0.101.2652.0 from Microsoft Store, says Always stay on top is enabled, and reports the Dock behind another normal or maximized application; fullscreen is explicitly an exception.
A community comment reports the reverse symptom in Command Palette version 0.11.11762.0: Always stay on top does not get disabled properly.
Maintainer zadjii-msft asked on 2026-10-14T11:09:33Z for the target application and whether the setup is multi-monitor. No author response follows; live labels include Needs-Author-Feedback.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for the reporter to name the target application and confirm monitor topology; then reproduce the ordinary/maximized/fullscreen transitions on a current build.

fix_assessment.rationale: The Dock code owns topmost state, but the requested target-window and monitor facts are needed to identify which transition fails. No specific code change can be justified before that reproduction; this does not claim the reported behavior is expected or resolved.

issue_context.summary: The Dock reportedly drops behind ordinary windows with Always stay on top enabled, while another commenter sees the inverse state transition; the maintainer needs the exact target app and monitor topology to reproduce a path.
known_information: Command Palette Dock 0.101.2652.0 from Microsoft Store; Always stay on top is enabled; the Dock goes behind a normal or maximized application.
Fullscreen behavior is explicitly intended as an exception, and the reporter says the issue is reproducible.
A separate commenter on 2026-10-11 reports Always stay on top not being disabled properly in Command Palette 0.11.11762.0.
Maintainer zadjii-msft asked for the target application and whether the setup is multi-monitor on 2026-10-14; those answers are absent. The issue has Needs-Author-Feedback and Needs-Triage labels.
inferences: The opposite reports may involve different activation/fullscreen or monitor transitions, but do not establish a shared root cause.
The current Dock implementation changes z-order based on AlwaysOnTop and a fullscreen/busy state flag; the target window and topology may distinguish which transition is involved.
issue_context.analysis: The existing maintainer request already targets the missing discriminators, so another generic request or speculative fix adds no value. The prior reproduction action should remain hidden while the reporter's specific answer is outstanding.
initial_investigation: At upstream source head 1b33221dfa19f30d71409eb550807883fb27283a, DockWindow.xaml.cs::UpdateTopmostState computes topmost state from the setting and fullscreen flag, then calls SetWindowPos with HWND_TOPMOST, HWND_NOTOPMOST, or HWND_BOTTOM. This code fact does not prove a defect without the requested transition details.
The existing #50766 artifact was generated on 2026-09-24 and contains a broad reproduction action; it predates the maintainer's current request and is not current evidence.
No exact #50766 issue, PR, or branch trace was found in MuyuanMS/PowerToys.
